state_cache_sizing.answer: --max-mamba-cache-size counts state SLOTS, not tokens and not per-layer entries. Each slot holds the full per-layer state of one sequence — the pool allocates tensors with an explicit layer dimension, so slot cost multiplies by the 24 linear layers. Concurrency is size // ratio with ratio = 3 by default (3 + 2 = 5 with extra_buffer and overlap scheduling), so slots, not KV tokens, bind first on a 4:1 hybrid.

state_cache_sizing.does_it_bind_first: Yes. KV cache grows with tokens and is shared across the whole sequence length; the state pool is a per-concurrent-sequence cost over 24 linear layers and does not shrink with NVFP4 weights (SSM/conv state dtype is separate, --mamba-ssm-dtype). With ratio 3, slots cap concurrency at size/3; long prompts make KV scarce while many short requests make slots scarce — on a 4:1 hybrid at high concurrency the slot cap arrives first.

flags.why: Only hard upstream constraint found is divisibility with the state tracking interval; 256 % 64 == 0 keeps the assert satisfied and matches the mamba chunk granularity. No explicit per-architecture recommendation exists upstream — treat 64 as the constrained-safe choice, not a documented optimum.

flags.why: extra_buffer is platform-gated and asserts; it also raises slots/request from 3 to 5, costing ~40% more state memory on a box that has none to spare. no_buffer avoids the gate entirely.

startup_risks.risk: State cache too small to admit a single request — hard RuntimeError during KV/state configuration, before the server ever listens.
startup_risks.evidence:
raise RuntimeError(
                    f"Hybrid (mamba/linear-attention) state cache is too small to serve "
                    f"any requests. max_mamba_cache_size={...}, "
startup_risks.mitigation: Set --max-mamba-cache-size explicitly and either raise --mem-fraction-static or halve state with --mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16.

startup_risks.risk: Unified-memory over-commit: another model is already resident, GB10 reports no discrete VRAM, and the auto mem fraction is sized against total device memory while the state pool is allocated before capture. Expect OOM or a wedged CUDA context rather than a clean error.
startup_risks.evidence: # Mamba state is a fixed pre-capture allocation, so it can't ride the ~0 post-capture slack.
startup_risks.mitigation: Explicit conservative --mem-fraction-static (0.5), explicit --max-running-requests, and one model per box for the first cell.

startup_risks.risk: Auto strategy resolving to extra_buffer on a platform that lacks support -> assertion at arg-validation time.
startup_risks.mitigation: Pass --mamba-radix-cache-strategy no_buffer explicitly instead of letting auto decide.
